title: A weird IPO pull, a tainted reputation and the stalled breakout moment for AI wearables
key_facts: Smart ring maker Oura withdrew its planned IPO, only days after formally launching it on 21 September.
It had planned to raise up to $2.2 billion by selling 50 million shares on Nasdaq at an implied market value of $15 billion.
Oura gave no reason; CEO Tom Hale said an IPO was 'one step in our journey' and the company had 'the luxury of choosing our moment'.
Silicon UK links the withdrawal to other pulled US IPOs amid rising interest rates; Holtec also postponed in September.
Oura is profitable: pre-tax profit $23.5m on sales of $907.8m in the year to 30 September 2025; revenue expected to grow 90% in fiscal 2026.
It sold about 3.6 million units in the past year and had more than five million paid members at 30 June, per its filing.
quote_evidence: Smart ring maker Oura has withdrawn its planned IPO, only days after formally launching the plans on 21 September.
Oura didn’t indicate why it was changing its plans, but it is the latest company to withdraw a major US IPO amid changing conditions, including rising central bank benchmark interest rates.
why_it_matters_hint: A well-known consumer health-tech firm backed away from listing; the reason is not given by the company.
event_date: Exact date of withdrawal not stated; reported by 3-4 Oct 2026
